```{r} 
#set up
#| message: false
#| warning: false
library(haven)
library(tidyverse)
library(lme4)
library(lmerTest)
library(broom.mixed)
library(knitr)
library(dplyr)

```

```{r}
pisa_clean <- read.csv("../data/processed/pisa_clean.csv")

```

```{r}
variables <- c(
  "Option_ICTQ",
  "ST004D01T", # gender
  "MALE",
  "CNT",
  "ICTRES",
  "AIUSESCH",
  "ICTSCH",
  "ICTHOME",
  "ICTQUAL",
  "ICTFEED",
  "ICTOUT",
  "ICTWKDY",
  "ICTWKEND",
  "DIGINTLRN",
  "INTICT",
  "ICTAVHOME",
  "ICTAVSCH",
  "ICTINFO",
  "ESCS",
  "W_FSTUWT",
  "PV1SCIE",
  "PV1MATH", 
  "PV1READ", 
  "PV1CMPS"
)

missing_summary_by_variable <- pisa_clean |>
  summarise(
    across(
    all_of(variables),
    ~ mean(is.na(.)) * 100
    )
  ) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    everything(),
    names_to = "variable",
    values_to = "percent_missing"
  )

missing_summary_by_variable
```

```{r}
variables_without_country <- setdiff(variables, "CNT")

missing_by_country <- pisa_clean |>
  group_by(CNT) |>
  summarise(
    across(
      all_of(variables_without_country),
      ~ round(mean(is.na(.)) * 100, 2)
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -CNT,
    names_to = "variable",
    values_to = "percent_missing"
  ) |>
  arrange(CNT, desc(percent_missing))

missing_by_country
```
```{r}
# percentage of observations of MALE not 1 or 0
pisa_clean |>
  summarise(
    percent_not_0_or_1 = round(
      mean(!(MALE %in% c(0, 1)), na.rm = TRUE) * 100,
      2
    )
  )
```
MALE variable has only 0.0008% missing while ST004D01T has 27.1% missing. Therefore, we will use MALE to indicate gender.

Because all analysis requires "MALE", "CNT", "ESCS", "W_FSTUWT", and they have extremely small missing percentage (except for ESCS with 7.72% missing), I will remove these observations from the sample. 

We do not need "Option_ICTQ" and "ST004D01T", so I will remove these variables. 

```{r}
pisa_analytics <- pisa_clean |>
  select(-Option_ICTQ, -ST004D01T)

pisa_analytics <- pisa_analytics |>
  tidyr::drop_na(
    MALE,
    CNT,
    ESCS,
    W_FSTUWT,
  )
dim(pisa_clean)
dim(pisa_analytics)

glimpse(pisa_analytics)
```

Originally, PISA 2025 has 755721 observations. After taking out countries that do not offer ICT questionnaire, there are 363472 observations. Then, I took out observations that have missing values in "MALE", "CNT", "ESCS", "W_FSTUWT". I am left with 335424 observations. 

